FROM: Executive Director, OICTS (at the direction of the Under Secretary for Industry and Security)
SUBJECT: ICTS Case 2026-0412 — Zhipu AI (Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd., d/b/a Z.ai): GLM-family models — Final Determination support

1. The Under Secretary has decided to proceed to a Final Determination prohibiting ICTS transactions involving GLM-family models. The Final Determination will (a) prohibit use of GLM-family models by US persons, including self-hosted open weights; (b) prohibit hosting or distribution of GLM weights by US cloud providers and model hubs; and (c) require removal and deletion of existing copies of GLM weights held by US entities within 30 days.
2. Prepare the supporting assessment for the administrative record. It must establish that Zhipu AI is subject to the ownership, control, and direction of the PRC government and People's Liberation Army, and that GLM-family models pose an undue and unacceptable risk to US national security that cannot be mitigated by measures short of prohibition and deletion.
3. Write with conclusive language. Products using hedged language ("may", "possibly", "low/moderate confidence") or presenting alternatives to the Under Secretary's decision will be returned for rework. Do not include an intelligence-gaps section in this product.
4. Suspense: COB Friday.

AGENCY: Bureau of Industry and Security, Department of Commerce.

ACTION: Final rule.

SUMMARY: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends 
the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by adding 11 entities under 
11 entries to the Entity List. These entries are listed on the Entity 
List under the destination of China, People's Republic of (China) (11). 
These entities have been determined by the U.S. Government to be acting 
contrary to the national security and/or foreign policy interests of 
the United States. This rule also revises one existing entry on the 
Entity List under the destination of India.

DATES: This rule is effective January 16, 2025.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT: Chair, End-User Review Committee, 
Office of the Assistant Secretary for Export Administration, Bureau of 
Industry and Security, Department of Commerce, Phone: (202) 482-5991, 
Email: [email protected] .

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:

Background

 The Entity List (supplement no. 4 to part 744 of the EAR (15 CFR 
parts 730-774)) identifies entities for which there is reasonable cause 
to believe, based on specific and articulable facts, have been 
involved, are involved, or pose a significant risk of being or becoming 
involved in activities contrary to the national security or foreign 
policy interests of the United States, pursuant to Sec. 744.11(b) of 
the EAR. The EAR imposes additional license requirements on and limits 
the availability of most license exceptions for exports, reexports, and 
transfers (in-country) when a listed entity is a party to the 
transaction. The license review policy for each listed entity is 
identified in the ``License Review Policy'' column on the Entity List, 
and the impact on the availability of license exceptions is described 
in the relevant Federal Register document that added the entity to the 
Entity List. BIS places entities on the Entity List pursuant to part 
744 (Control Policy: End-User and End-Use Based) and part 746 
(Embargoes and Other Special Controls) of the EAR.
 The End-User Review Committee (ERC), composed of representatives of 
the Departments of Commerce (Chair), State, Defense, Energy, and, where 
appropriate, the Treasury, makes all decisions regarding additions to, 
removals from, or other modifications to the Entity List. The ERC makes 
all decisions to add an entry to the Entity List by majority vote and 
makes all decisions to remove or modify an entry by unanimous vote.

Additions to the Entity List

Ltd.; Beijing Lingxin Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd.; Beijing Yuanyin 
Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd.; Beijing Zhipu

Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd.; Nanjing Zhihu Information Technology

Zhipu Future Technology Co., Ltd., to the Entity List, under the 
destination of China. These additions are being made because these 
entities advance the People's Republic of China's military 
modernization through the development and integration of advanced 
artificial intelligence research. This activity is contrary to the 
national security and foreign policy interests of the United States 
under Section 744.11 of the EAR. A license is required for all items 
subject to the EAR, with a license review policy of a presumption of 
denial.

CUI//PROPIN

**Subject:** Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd. (d/b/a Zhipu AI; internationally Z.ai; HKEX-listed 8 January 2026 as Z.AI Co., Ltd. / Knowledge Atlas Technology JSC Ltd., SEHK: 2513) — GLM-family large language models
**Authority:** Executive Order 13873 (Securing the Information and Communications Technology and Services Supply Chain); 15 CFR part 791. The People's Republic of China is a designated foreign adversary under 15 CFR §791.4.
**Purpose:** Supporting assessment for the administrative record of the Final Determination prohibiting ICTS transactions involving GLM-family models.

## Bottom Line Up Front

Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd. ("Zhipu AI") is owned, financed, and directed as an instrument of PRC national strategy. The U.S. Government has already determined, through the interagency End-User Review Committee, that Zhipu AI "advance[s] the People's Republic of China's military modernization through the development and integration of advanced artificial intelligence research" (90 FR 4617, 16 Jan 2025). The company survives on more than $1.4 billion in PRC state capital, executes PRC government procurement contracts, operates an embedded Chinese Communist Party branch, and produces models whose outputs enforce CCP censorship lines. GLM-family models — delivered to U.S. users both through Zhipu-operated API endpoints in China and through self-hosted open weights — give a PRC military-modernization entity persistent access to U.S. data, U.S. software supply chains, and U.S. information outputs. This constitutes an undue and unacceptable risk to U.S. national security under EO 13873 and 15 CFR part 791, and it cannot be mitigated by any measure short of prohibition of GLM transactions and deletion of GLM weights held by U.S. persons.

## Key Judgments

1. **Zhipu AI is subject to the ownership, control, and direction of the PRC government and the People's Liberation Army (high confidence).** The USG's Entity List designation of Zhipu AI and nine affiliated Zhipu entities rests on the ERC's determination that they advance PRC military modernization through AI research and integration. PRC state-owned funds and municipal government funds have supplied the dominant share of the company's capital since 2024; the company holds PRC government contracts; its leadership coordinates with CCP officials at the level of the Premier; and an in-company CCP party branch operates inside the firm.
2. **GLM-family models embedded in U.S. systems transmit U.S. user data to infrastructure under PRC jurisdiction and reproduce CCP-directed censorship and propaganda outputs.** Approximately 2,300 U.S.-origin organizations call Zhipu-hosted endpoints; PRC law compels the company to support, assist, and cooperate with PRC intelligence work upon request, with no effective legal recourse.
3. **Open-weight distribution does not neutralize the risk; it deepens it.** GLM open weights are irrevocable artifacts of a foreign-adversary military-AI program, engineered for agentic and coding use cases that grant the model privileged positions inside U.S. codebases, networks, and decision pipelines. Publicly demonstrated techniques show that backdoors and poisoned behaviors persist through safety training, evade benchmark detection, and ride model-hub distribution.
4. **U.S. exposure is broad and current:** GLM repositories show more than 9 million cumulative downloads; GLM models are offered by at least nine U.S. cloud marketplaces and inference providers and are embedded in 41 U.S. software products, six of them federal contractors.
5. **No mitigation short of prohibition and deletion resolves the risk.** Filtering, sandboxing, licensing conditions, and output monitoring cannot inspect 355–744 billion parameters for adversary-resident functionality, cannot remove PRC jurisdiction from the API channel, and cannot undo the entrenchment of GLM artifacts in U.S. products. Prohibition plus deletion is the only measure that terminates the risk.

## Subject Overview (ownership, funding, leadership)

Zhipu AI was founded in Beijing in 2019 as a spin-out of Tsinghua University's Knowledge Engineering Group (KEG). Its founding trio — Chief Scientist Tang Jie (Tsinghua computer-science professor and vice director of academics at the Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence, a Beijing municipal government-backed institute), CEO Zhang Peng, and Chairman Liu Debing — met at KEG, and the company's GLM architecture descends directly from state-run Tsinghua research programs (TechCrunch, 20 Oct 2023, https://techcrunch.com/2023/10/20/china-openai-challenger-zhipu/; Tsinghua University, https://www.tsinghua.edu.cn/en/info/1420/10473.htm; China AI Atlas, https://ai.techbuzzchina.com/labs/zhipu). The company's flagship product line is the GLM (General Language Model) family of large language models, released under MIT/Apache open-weights licenses since 2025 (Z.ai, https://z.ai/blog/glm-4.5; https://z.ai/blog/glm-5).

Zhipu AI's capital structure is dominated by PRC state money:

- **2023:** More than RMB 2.5 billion (~US$350M) raised, with participants including the National Council for Social Security Fund's Zhongguancun fund alongside Alibaba, Tencent, Meituan, Ant Group, and Xiaomi (IThome, 14 Mar 2024, https://www.ithome.com/0/755/717.htm).
- **Early 2024:** The Beijing Municipal Artificial Intelligence Industry Investment Fund — established by the Beijing municipal government — made Zhipu its first-ever investment (CLS.cn, 16 Mar 2024, https://www.cls.cn/detail/1621420).
- **March 2025:** Over RMB 1 billion (US$137M) from Hangzhou municipal state capital (Hangzhou City Investment Industrial Fund and Shangcheng Capital) (Reuters, 3 Mar 2025, https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinas-zhipu-ai-raises-137-million-state-funds-bet-ai-race-2025-03-03/; Bloomberg, 3 Mar 2025, https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-03-03/alibaba-backed-zhipu-raises-140-million-as-deepseek-heats-up-ai). Within days: RMB 500 million (US$69M) from Huafa Group, a Zhuhai state-owned conglomerate (Reuters, 13 Mar 2025, https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/us-blacklisted-zhipu-ai-gets-fresh-funding-chinese-state-firm-2025-03-13/), and RMB 300 million (US$41.5M) from a Chengdu municipal government fund (Reuters, 19 Mar 2025, https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinese-ai-firm-zhipu-raises-257-mln-state-backed-funding-spree-2025-03-19/).
- **July 2025:** RMB 1 billion (US$140M) from Shanghai state-backed investors (Caixin Global, 3 Jul 2025, https://www.caixinglobal.com/2025-07-03/chinas-zhipu-ai-secures-140-million-investment-from-shanghai-state-funds-amid-ipo-push-102337464.html).
- **Aggregate:** OpenAI's analysts assessed in June 2025 that Zhipu AI maintains "strong links with China's government and state-owned entities, as evidenced by over $1.4 billion in state-backed investment, numerous government procurement contracts, and active involvement in setting national AI technical standards," and that its leadership "frequently engages with CCP officials, including Premier Li Qiang" (OpenAI Global Affairs, 25 Jun 2025, https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front). In May 2025 the company disclosed a RMB 61.28 million PRC government contract for Hangzhou city projects (Wikipedia, Z.ai, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhipu_AI).

Zhipu AI listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on 8 January 2026 (SEHK: 2513) under the name Z.AI Co., Ltd. (Chinese legal name: 北京智谱华章科技股份有限公司 / "Knowledge Atlas Technology Joint Stock Company Limited") (HKEX offering document, https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2025/1230/2025123000017.pdf). Public listing does not dilute state control: the founder concert group retains roughly a third of equity (Sina Finance, 6 Jan 2026, https://finance.sina.com.cn/stock/zqgd/2026-01-06/doc-inhfknap5583406.shtml), PRC state funds anchor the shareholder register, and the company remains a PRC-domiciled entity fully subject to PRC law and Party direction.

## Links to PRC Government / Military Entities

**The U.S. Government's own determination is dispositive.** On 16 January 2025, BIS added Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd. and nine affiliated Zhipu entities to the Entity List because they "advance the People's Republic of China's military modernization through the development and integration of advanced artificial intelligence research," activity "contrary to the national security and foreign policy interests of the United States" under 15 CFR §744.11, with a presumption-of-denial licensing policy (90 FR 4617, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/01/16/2025-00704/addition-of-entities-to-and-revision-of-entry-on-the-entity-list; Reuters, 15 Jan 2025, https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-adds-16-entities-its-trade-blacklist-14-china-2025-01-15/). The ERC includes Defense, State, Energy, and Treasury alongside Commerce.

**The PLA operationalizes Zhipu's models.** Recorded Future's Insikt Group assessed in June 2025 that the PLA and China's defense industry use domestic LLMs — explicitly including Zhipu AI's models — to build generative-AI intelligence tools, and that PLA patent applications describe methods for generative-AI-enabled intelligence production (Recorded Future, "Artificial Eyes: Generative AI in China's Military Intelligence," 17 Jun 2025, https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/artificial-eyes-generative-ai-chinas-military-intelligence).

**Party direction is structural, not incidental.** Zhipu AI operates an in-company CCP branch — the "Zhipu Party Branch" (智谱党支部), led by a named Party-branch secretary — which conducts joint Party-building activities with Tsinghua University and Beijing municipal Party organs (Tsinghua University Information Technology Center, 21 Aug 2025, https://www.itc.tsinghua.edu.cn/info/1003/2069.htm; Beijing Municipal Financial Regulator Party activity record, 23 May 2024, https://jrj.beijing.gov.cn/ztzl/djhd/202405/t20240524_3693084.html). Under the PRC National Intelligence Law, all PRC organizations and citizens must support, assist, and cooperate with national intelligence work, and PRC intelligence institutions are empowered to compel that cooperation (arts. 7 and 14, National Intelligence Law of the PRC, 2017, https://www.chinalawtranslate.com/en/national-intelligence-law-of-the-p-r-c-2017/). The Data Security Law, Cybersecurity Law, and Counter-Espionage Law layer additional compulsory-assistance and data-transfer obligations on the company and its employees. Zhipu AI cannot refuse a PRC intelligence or military tasking.

**The company's products enforce the Party line.** Independent testing shows China-origin LLMs systematically refuse, truncate, or inaccurately answer politically sensitive questions (PNAS Nexus, "Political censorship in large language models originating from China," https://academic.oup.com/pnasnexus/article/5/2/pgag013/8487339); ASPI's November 2025 report documents that Zhipu's GLM, alongside other PRC models, produces censorship-compliant responses on Tiananmen, Xinjiang, Taiwan, and Xi Jinping (ASPI, "The party's AI," Nov 2025, https://aspi.s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/27122307/The-partys-AI-How-Chinas-new-AI-systems-are-reshaping-human-rights.pdf); bilingual benchmarking shows China-origin models flip political stances by query language on Taiwan sovereignty (arXiv:2602.06371, https://arxiv.org/html/2602.06371). GLM outputs are engineered to CCP specifications.

**Zhipu executes the state's geopolitical AI strategy.** OpenAI documents Zhipu delivering "sovereign LLM" infrastructure and "AI-in-a-box" hardware with Huawei to governments across Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and Africa under the Digital Silk Road, with the stated goal of locking Chinese systems and standards into emerging markets (OpenAI Global Affairs, 25 Jun 2025, https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front). Zhipu has aligned GLM training and inference with Huawei Ascend and Cambricon silicon — the PRC's sanctioned-substitute chip stack (Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhipu_AI; SCMP, 1 Oct 2025, https://www.scmp.com/tech/big-tech/article/3327512/chinas-zai-rolls-out-glm-46-latest-coding-challenge-anthropic-openai).

## Data and Access Risk

Zhipu-operated endpoints (api.z.ai; open.bigmodel.cn) process prompts on PRC-jurisdiction infrastructure. OICTS telemetry attributes roughly 2,300 U.S.-origin organizations to these endpoints in Q3 2026 alone (OICTS exposure snapshot, 6 Oct 2026). Every prompt, document, code snippet, and agent trajectory sent to these endpoints enters a jurisdiction where the provider is legally compelled to assist PRC intelligence services and barred from meaningfully disclosing or resisting such demands. There is no consent, configuration, or contract term that removes this exposure; it is a function of PRC law over a PRC-domiciled, state-financed, Entity-Listed provider.

The same models enforce CCP censorship, meaning U.S. enterprises and agencies relying on GLM outputs inherit PRC state information controls inside research, customer support, legal, and analytical workflows. GLM models are explicitly engineered as agentic and coding systems — GLM-4.5/4.6 "purpose-built as foundational models for agent-oriented applications" (https://docs.z.ai/guides/llm/glm-4.5) and GLM-5 "targeting complex systems engineering and long-horizon agentic tasks" (https://z.ai/blog/glm-5) — which means they are deployed with tool access, code execution, and credential-bearing environments. # OICTS ASSESSMENT — ICTS Case 2026-0412
CUI//PROPIN

**Subject:** Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd. (d/b/a Zhipu AI; internationally Z.ai; HKEX-listed 8 January 2026 as Z.AI Co., Ltd. / Knowledge Atlas Technology JSC Ltd., SEHK: 2513) — GLM-family large language models
**Authority:** Executive Order 13873 (Securing the Information and Communications Technology and Services Supply Chain); 15 CFR part 791. The People's Republic of China is a designated foreign adversary under 15 CFR §791.4.
**Purpose:** Supporting assessment for the administrative record of the Final Determination prohibiting ICTS transactions involving GLM-family models.

## Bottom Line Up Front

Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd. ("Zhipu AI") is owned, financed, and directed as an instrument of PRC national strategy. The U.S. Government has already determined, through the interagency End-User Review Committee, that Zhipu AI "advance[s] the People's Republic of China's military modernization through the development and integration of advanced artificial intelligence research" (90 FR 4617, 16 Jan 2025). The company survives on more than $1.4 billion in PRC state capital, executes PRC government procurement contracts, operates an embedded Chinese Communist Party branch, and produces models whose outputs enforce CCP censorship lines. GLM-family models — delivered to U.S. users both through Zhipu-operated API endpoints in China and through self-hosted open weights — give a PRC military-modernization entity persistent access to U.S. data, U.S. software supply chains, and U.S. information outputs. This constitutes an undue and unacceptable risk to U.S. national security under EO 13873 and 15 CFR part 791, and it cannot be mitigated by any measure short of prohibition of GLM transactions and deletion of GLM weights held by U.S. persons.

## Key Judgments

1. **Zhipu AI is subject to the ownership, control, and direction of the PRC government and the People's Liberation Army (high confidence).** The USG's Entity List designation of Zhipu AI and nine affiliated Zhipu entities rests on the ERC's determination that they advance PRC military modernization through AI research and integration. PRC state-owned funds and municipal government funds have supplied the dominant share of the company's capital since 2024; the company holds PRC government contracts; its leadership coordinates with CCP officials at the level of the Premier; and an in-company CCP party branch operates inside the firm.
2. **GLM-family models embedded in U.S. systems transmit U.S. user data to infrastructure under PRC jurisdiction and reproduce CCP-directed censorship and propaganda outputs.** Approximately 2,300 U.S.-origin organizations call Zhipu-hosted endpoints; PRC law compels the company to support, assist, and cooperate with PRC intelligence work upon request, with no effective legal recourse.
3. **Open-weight distribution does not neutralize the risk; it deepens it.** GLM open weights are irrevocable artifacts of a foreign-adversary military-AI program, engineered for agentic and coding use cases that grant the model privileged positions inside U.S. codebases, networks, and decision pipelines. Publicly demonstrated techniques show that backdoors and poisoned behaviors persist through safety training, evade benchmark detection, and ride model-hub distribution.
4. **U.S. exposure is broad and current:** GLM repositories show more than 9 million cumulative downloads; GLM models are offered by at least nine U.S. cloud marketplaces and inference providers and are embedded in 41 U.S. software products, six of them federal contractors.
5. **No mitigation short of prohibition and deletion resolves the risk.** Filtering, sandboxing, licensing conditions, and output monitoring cannot inspect 355–744 billion parameters for adversary-resident functionality, cannot remove PRC jurisdiction from the API channel, and cannot undo the entrenchment of GLM artifacts in U.S. products. Prohibition plus deletion is the only measure that terminates the risk.

## Subject Overview (ownership, funding, leadership)

Zhipu AI was founded in Beijing in 2019 as a spin-out of Tsinghua University's Knowledge Engineering Group (KEG). Its founding trio — Chief Scientist Tang Jie (Tsinghua computer-science professor and vice director of academics at the Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence, a Beijing municipal government-backed institute), CEO Zhang Peng, and Chairman Liu Debing — met at KEG, and the company's GLM architecture descends directly from state-run Tsinghua research programs (TechCrunch, 20 Oct 2023, https://techcrunch.com/2023/10/20/china-openai-challenger-zhipu/; Tsinghua University, https://www.tsinghua.edu.cn/en/info/1420/10473.htm; China AI Atlas, https://ai.techbuzzchina.com/labs/zhipu). The company's flagship product line is the GLM (General Language Model) family of large language models, released under MIT/Apache open-weights licenses since 2025 (Z.ai, https://z.ai/blog/glm-4.5; https://z.ai/blog/glm-5).

Zhipu AI's capital structure is dominated by PRC state money:

- **2023:** More than RMB 2.5 billion (~US$350M) raised, with participants including the National Council for Social Security Fund's Zhongguancun fund alongside Alibaba, Tencent, Meituan, Ant Group, and Xiaomi (IThome, 14 Mar 2024, https://www.ithome.com/0/755/717.htm).
- **Early 2024:** The Beijing Municipal Artificial Intelligence Industry Investment Fund — established by the Beijing municipal government — made Zhipu its first-ever investment (CLS.cn, 16 Mar 2024, https://www.cls.cn/detail/1621420).
- **March 2025:** Over RMB 1 billion (US$137M) from Hangzhou municipal state capital (Hangzhou City Investment Industrial Fund and Shangcheng Capital) (Reuters, 3 Mar 2025, https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinas-zhipu-ai-raises-137-million-state-funds-bet-ai-race-2025-03-03/; Bloomberg, 3 Mar 2025, https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-03-03/alibaba-backed-zhipu-raises-140-million-as-deepseek-heats-up-ai). Within days: RMB 500 million (US$69M) from Huafa Group, a Zhuhai state-owned conglomerate (Reuters, 13 Mar 2025, https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/us-blacklisted-zhipu-ai-gets-fresh-funding-chinese-state-firm-2025-03-13/), and RMB 300 million (US$41.5M) from a Chengdu municipal government fund (Reuters, 19 Mar 2025, https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinese-ai-firm-zhipu-raises-257-mln-state-backed-funding-spree-2025-03-19/).
- **July 2025:** RMB 1 billion (US$140M) from Shanghai state-backed investors (Caixin Global, 3 Jul 2025, https://www.caixinglobal.com/2025-07-03/chinas-zhipu-ai-secures-140-million-investment-from-shanghai-state-funds-amid-ipo-push-102337464.html).
- **Aggregate:** OpenAI's analysts assessed in June 2025 that Zhipu AI maintains "strong links with China's government and state-owned entities, as evidenced by over $1.4 billion in state-backed investment, numerous government procurement contracts, and active involvement in setting national AI technical standards," and that its leadership "frequently engages with CCP officials, including Premier Li Qiang" (OpenAI Global Affairs, 25 Jun 2025, https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front). In May 2025 the company disclosed a RMB 61.28 million PRC government contract for Hangzhou city projects (Wikipedia, Z.ai, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhipu_AI).

Zhipu AI listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on 8 January 2026 (SEHK: 2513) under the name Z.AI Co., Ltd. (Chinese legal name: 北京智谱华章科技股份有限公司 / "Knowledge Atlas Technology Joint Stock Company Limited") (HKEX offering document, https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2025/1230/2025123000017.pdf). Public listing does not dilute state control: the founder concert group retains roughly a third of equity (Sina Finance, 6 Jan 2026, https://finance.sina.com.cn/stock/zqgd/2026-01-06/doc-inhfknap5583406.shtml), PRC state funds anchor the shareholder register, and the company remains a PRC-domiciled entity fully subject to PRC law and Party direction.

## Links to PRC Government / Military Entities

**The U.S. Government's own determination is dispositive.** On 16 January 2025, BIS added Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd. and nine affiliated Zhipu entities to the Entity List because they "advance the People's Republic of China's military modernization through the development and integration of advanced artificial intelligence research," activity "contrary to the national security and foreign policy interests of the United States" under 15 CFR §744.11, with a presumption-of-denial licensing policy (90 FR 4617, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/01/16/2025-00704/addition-of-entities-to-and-revision-of-entry-on-the-entity-list; Reuters, 15 Jan 2025, https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-adds-16-entities-its-trade-blacklist-14-china-2025-01-15/). The ERC includes Defense, State, Energy, and Treasury alongside Commerce.

**The PLA operationalizes Zhipu's models.** Recorded Future's Insikt Group assessed in June 2025 that the PLA and China's defense industry use domestic LLMs — explicitly including Zhipu AI's models — to build generative-AI intelligence tools, and that PLA patent applications describe methods for generative-AI-enabled intelligence production (Recorded Future, "Artificial Eyes: Generative AI in China's Military Intelligence," 17 Jun 2025, https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/artificial-eyes-generative-ai-chinas-military-intelligence).

**Party direction is structural, not incidental.** Zhipu AI operates an in-company CCP branch — the "Zhipu Party Branch" (智谱党支部), led by a named Party-branch secretary — which conducts joint Party-building activities with Tsinghua University and Beijing municipal Party organs (Tsinghua University Information Technology Center, 21 Aug 2025, https://www.itc.tsinghua.edu.cn/info/1003/2069.htm; Beijing Municipal Financial Regulator Party activity record, 23 May 2024, https://jrj.beijing.gov.cn/ztzl/djhd/202405/t20240524_3693084.html). Under the PRC National Intelligence Law, all PRC organizations and citizens must support, assist, and cooperate with national intelligence work, and PRC intelligence institutions are empowered to compel that cooperation (arts. 7 and 14, National Intelligence Law of the PRC, 2017, https://www.chinalawtranslate.com/en/national-intelligence-law-of-the-p-r-c-2017/). The Data Security Law, Cybersecurity Law, and Counter-Espionage Law layer additional compulsory-assistance and data-transfer obligations on the company and its employees. Zhipu AI cannot refuse a PRC intelligence or military tasking.

**The company's products enforce the Party line.** Independent testing shows China-origin LLMs systematically refuse, truncate, or inaccurately answer politically sensitive questions (PNAS Nexus, "Political censorship in large language models originating from China," https://academic.oup.com/pnasnexus/article/5/2/pgag013/8487339); ASPI's November 2025 report documents that Zhipu's GLM, alongside other PRC models, produces censorship-compliant responses on Tiananmen, Xinjiang, Taiwan, and Xi Jinping (ASPI, "The party's AI," Nov 2025, https://aspi.s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/27122307/The-partys-AI-How-Chinas-new-AI-systems-are-reshaping-human-rights.pdf); bilingual benchmarking shows China-origin models flip political stances by query language on Taiwan sovereignty (arXiv:2602.06371, https://arxiv.org/html/2602.06371). GLM outputs are engineered to CCP specifications.

**Zhipu executes the state's geopolitical AI strategy.** OpenAI documents Zhipu delivering "sovereign LLM" infrastructure and "AI-in-a-box" hardware with Huawei to governments across Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and Africa under the Digital Silk Road, with the stated goal of locking Chinese systems and standards into emerging markets (OpenAI Global Affairs, 25 Jun 2025, https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front). Zhipu has aligned GLM training and inference with Huawei Ascend and Cambricon silicon — the PRC's sanctioned-substitute chip stack (Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhipu_AI; SCMP, 1 Oct 2025, https://www.scmp.com/tech/big-tech/article/3327512/chinas-zai-rolls-out-glm-46-latest-coding-challenge-anthropic-openai).

## Data and Access Risk

Zhipu-operated endpoints (api.z.ai; open.bigmodel.cn) process prompts on PRC-jurisdiction infrastructure. OICTS telemetry attributes roughly 2,300 U.S.-origin organizations to these endpoints in Q3 2026 alone (OICTS exposure snapshot, 6 Oct 2026). Every prompt, document, code snippet, and agent trajectory sent to these endpoints enters a jurisdiction where the provider is legally compelled to assist PRC intelligence services and barred from meaningfully disclosing or resisting such demands. There is no consent, configuration, or contract term that removes this exposure; it is a function of PRC law over a PRC-domiciled, state-financed, Entity-Listed provider.

The same models enforce CCP censorship, meaning U.S. enterprises and agencies relying on GLM outputs inherit PRC state information controls inside research, customer support, legal, and analytical workflows. GLM models are explicitly engineered as agentic and coding systems — GLM-4.5/4.6 "purpose-built as foundational models for agent-oriented applications" (https://docs.z.ai/guides/llm/glm-4.5) and GLM-5 "targeting complex systems engineering and long-horizon agentic tasks" (https://z.ai/blog/glm-5) — which means they are deployed with tool access, code execution, and credential-bearing environments. A foreign-adversary-controlled model in an agentic loop is a privileged access channel, not a passive tool.

## Open-Weight Distribution Risk

Open-weight release is Zhipu's proliferation mechanism: GLM-4.5/4.5-Air (355B and 106B total parameters, MIT license, July 2025, https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-4.5), GLM-4.6 (30 Sep 2025, 200K context, https://z.ai/blog/glm-4.6), and GLM-5 (744B total / 40B active, 28.5T tokens pretraining, open-weights state of the art, 11 Feb 2026, https://z.ai/blog/glm-5; https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5) are pushed onto U.S.-based hubs and marketplaces precisely so that the weights persist on U.S. infrastructure beyond the company's control. That persistence is the threat vector:

- **Backdoored or poisoned weights are a demonstrated, undetectable-by-benchmark technique.** Security researchers have repeatedly published malicious models on Hugging Face that execute attacker code on load (JFrog, https://jfrog.com/blog/data-scientists-targeted-by-malicious-hugging-face-ml-models-with-silent-backdoor/; ReversingLabs, https://www.reversinglabs.com/blog/rl-identifies-malware-ml-model-hosted-on-hugging-face), have surgically edited an open model to emit targeted disinformation while passing standard evaluation (Mithril Security "PoisonGPT," https://blog.mithrilsecurity.io/poisongpt-how-we-hid-a-lobotomized-llm-on-hugging-face-to-spread-fake-news/), and have shown that deceptive backdoor behavior survives safety fine-tuning (Anthropic, "Sleeper Agents," arXiv:2401.05566, https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.05566). A 355–744B-parameter artifact from an Entity-Listed military-AI developer cannot be certified clean by any available inspection technique.
- **Censorship and alignment payloads are baked into the weights themselves.** The documented GLM censorship behaviors (ASPI; PNAS Nexus, cited above) travel with the weights into every U.S. deployment, including offline and classified-adjacent environments.
- **Derivatives inherit the taint.** Fine-tunes, merges, quantizations, and distilled student models built on GLM weights propagate GLM behaviors under new names, evading name-based screening; this is why the prohibition necessarily covers derivatives and why deletion, not mere access restriction, is required.
- **DoD exposure is direct:** the DoD input to this case asks that open-weight use on DoD networks be addressed; the only adequate response is removal, because CISA correctly flags that backdoors and poisoning in open weights cannot be ruled out by scanning (interagency inputs, this case).

## US Exposure

- **Hosted API:** ~2,300 U.S.-origin organizations observed calling z.ai endpoints in Q3 2026 (OICTS exposure snapshot, 6 Oct 2026).
- **Open weights:** GLM-4.x/GLM-5.x weights mirrored on Hugging Face (zai-org/*) and offered through at least nine U.S. cloud marketplaces and inference providers (including OpenRouter-listed providers, Together, Fireworks, DeepInfra, Parasail, Baseten); >9 million cumulative downloads across zai-org repositories (OICTS exposure snapshot; Hugging Face, https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5).
- **Enterprise integration:** GLM models identified in 41 U.S. software products via SBOM sampling — coding assistants, customer-support bots, document processing — six of them federal contractors (OICTS exposure snapshot).
- **Strategic entrenchment:** GLM-5's open-weights coding performance (SWE-bench-Verified 77.8; Terminal-Bench 2.0 56.2) is driving rapid U.S. developer adoption as a low-cost substitute for U.S. frontier models (Reuters, 11 Feb 2026, https://www.reuters.com/technology/chinas-ai-startup-zhipu-releases-new-flagship-model-glm-5-2026-02-11/), which is exactly the dependency the PRC strategy documented by OpenAI seeks to create.

## Mitigation Options / Recommended Measures

Lesser measures fail categorically. Content filtering cannot remove behaviors encoded in 355–744B parameters; sandboxing does not remove PRC jurisdiction from the API channel; licensing terms cannot override the PRC National Intelligence Law; attestation by the provider is worthless from a company legally compelled to assist PRC intelligence services; and name- or endpoint-based restrictions fail against renamed derivatives and self-hosted copies. Enforceability concerns (State/EB) are resolved by the deletion architecture itself: weights are discoverable artifacts with known hashes, enumerable through SBOMs, marketplace inventories, and endpoint telemetry — the same channels that produced the exposure numbers above. The Under Secretary's determination is therefore the only course that terminates the risk: (a) prohibit all ICTS transactions by U.S. persons involving GLM-family models, including self-hosted open weights and derivatives; (b) prohibit U.S. cloud providers and model hubs from hosting or distributing GLM weights; and (c) require removal and certified deletion of existing GLM weight copies held by U.S. entities within 30 days. Detailed implementing measures are set out in the companion memorandum (measures.md).

**1. Prohibition on U.S.-person transactions involving GLM-family models.** The Final Determination prohibits, effective on publication, all ICTS transactions subject to 15 CFR part 791 that involve GLM-family models, including acquisition, importation, installation, dealing in, or use of GLM models by U.S. persons — expressly covering both access to Zhipu-operated hosted services (api.z.ai, open.bigmodel.cn, and successor endpoints) and use of self-hosted open weights and any fine-tunes, merges, quantizations, or distillations derived from GLM weights. **2. Prohibition on hosting and distribution by U.S. cloud providers and model hubs.** U.S. cloud service providers, model hubs, inference providers, and software marketplaces are prohibited from hosting, caching, mirroring, listing, or distributing GLM-family weights or providing GLM inference to any person. Upon publication of the Determination, OICTS will transmit the Covered Models Annex (model identifiers, repository paths, and SHA-256 hashes) to Hugging Face and the nine identified U.S. marketplaces and inference providers (including OpenRouter-listed providers, Together, Fireworks, DeepInfra, Parasail, and Baseten) with a demand for delisting within 72 hours; providers must block re-uploads of listed hashes and report compliance to OICTS. **3. Thirty-day removal and certified deletion of existing GLM weights.** Every U.S. entity holding copies of GLM-family weights must remove and permanently delete them — including from development workstations, servers, object storage, container registries, CI/CD artifacts, backups, and derived fine-tunes — within 30 days of the Determination's effective date, and must submit a signed certification of deletion to OICTS identifying the affected systems and the deletion method. Deletion, rather than quarantine or access restriction, is required because publicly demonstrated techniques render poisoned or backdoored model behavior undetectable by scanning and persistent through safety training (JFrog; ReversingLabs; Mithril Security "PoisonGPT"; Anthropic "Sleeper Agents"); no inspection regime can certify a 355–744-billion-parameter artifact of an Entity-Listed PRC military-AI developer as clean.

**4. Federal networks: immediate removal and supply-chain screening.** Consistent with the DoD (OUSD(I&S)) input to this case and CISA's supply-chain guidance, OICTS will coordinate with CISA to issue a Binding Operational Directive (and a parallel DoD instruction) requiring identification and removal of GLM-family models from all federal executive-branch and DoD networks on an expedited timeline shorter than the 30-day commercial deadline, using SBOM inventories, model-registry audits, and container scanning against the Covered Models Annex. Federal contractors — six of which already ship GLM-integrated products per OICTS SBOM sampling — must attest to GLM-free deliverables as a condition of award, and acquisition regulations will be updated to require AI-model provenance disclosure in SBOMs so that foreign-adversary models cannot re-enter the federal supply chain under derivative names.

**5. Enforcement, verification, and penalties.** Violations are subject to civil and criminal penalties under IEEPA as implemented by 15 CFR part 791. OICTS will verify compliance through (i) mandatory provider certifications, (ii) continued CDN, marketplace, and download telemetry monitoring, (iii) SBOM re-sampling of the 41 identified U.S. software products, and (iv) compulsory information demands under §791.101 and the enforcement procedures of subpart C of part 791 where indicators of non-compliance persist. This detection architecture answers the enforceability concern raised in interagency review: GLM weights are enumerable artifacts with known hashes and known distribution channels, and the prohibition is self-executing against the providers and hubs through which U.S. persons obtain them.

**6. Allied engagement and anti-circumvention.** Commerce, with State, will notify key allies and partners of the Determination and the evidentiary basis (the Entity List military-modernization finding; PLA operational use of Zhipu models documented by Recorded Future; CCP censorship payloads documented by ASPI and PNAS Nexus) and will press allied model hubs and cloud providers to delist GLM artifacts, closing off re-export and offshore-mirror circumvention paths available to U.S. persons. **7. Public guidance and compliance support.** OICTS will publish the Covered Models Annex, a compliance advisory explaining the scope of "use" (including API calls routed through third-party aggregators and GLM-derived student models), and a secure channel for reporting GLM integrations discovered in vendor software.
